locator: I.16 [7]: some being that is only in act and in no wise in potency
interpretation: We see something emerge from potency to act; it does not bring itself to act, so a prior being brings it; this cannot go on to infinity; so there is some being only in act and in no way in potency, 'This being we call God'. Read as an existence conclusion over the series of beings that bring others from potency to act. Taken strictly, the regress premise only yields a first such being that is not itself brought to act by another; that it has no potency at all needs the further premise of [3] that whatever is in some way in potency has something prior to it. The argument runs from motion to pure act without the first-being bridge, but it concludes to existence, not that every first unmoved mover is pure act. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
